items.stem:
Consider the following statements
(i) The sex of a child is determined by what it inherits from the mother.
(ii) The sex of a child is determined by what it inherits from the father.
(iii) The probability of having a male child is more than that of a female child.
(iv) The sex of a child is determined at the time of fertilisation when male and female gametes fuse to form a zygote.
The correct statements are :
items.answer: A child who inherits an X chromosome from her father will be a girl and one who inherits a Y chromosome from him will be a boy. The sex is therefore decided by the father's contribution at the moment of fertilisation. Thus (b) is the correct option.

items.stem: Each gamete carries only one allele. This is proposed in which law ?
items.answer: During gamete formation, the alleles for each gene segregate from each other so that each gamete carries only one allele for each gene. This was proposed in the law of segregation. Thus (b) is the correct option.
items.ocr: MinerU dropped the printed question number; it is inferred as 4 from its position between questions 3 and 5 on page 3.

items.stem: Structure present in a cell which is responsible for determination of the sex of a baby is :
items.answer: Human cells have two types of chromosomes: autosomes and sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes in a male are XY and in a female they are XX. There are no differences in the cytoplasm or membrane, and the chromosome is present inside the nucleus. Thus (d) is the correct option.
items.ocr: Option label for 'cytoplasm' was OCR'd as a bare 'C' ('C cytoplasm'); restored to option (A) because (b), (c) and (d) are printed intact after it.

items.stem: Which of the following is the father of genetics ?
items.answer: Gregor Mendel discovered the fundamental laws of inheritance by working on pea plants. He deduced that genes come in pairs and are inherited as distinct units, one from each parent. Mendel tracked the segregation of parental genes and their appearance in the offspring as dominant or recessive traits. He was the first person to figure out genetics well enough to be able to predict the results of the crosses that he made. Some of his findings included the ideas of dominant and recessive factors, independent assortment and segregation of alleles. Thus (a) is the correct option.
items.ocr: Stem printed as 'Which of the following the father of genetics ?'; the dropped verb 'is' was restored.

items.stem: Which of the following statement for chromosomal theory of inheritance is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Pairing and separation of a pair of the chromosomes would lead to segregation of a factor they carried.

options.label: B
options.text: Behaviour of chromosomes is parallel to the behaviour of genes.

options.label: C
options.text: The two alleles of a gene pair are located on homologous sites on homologous chromosomes.

options.label: D
options.text: Chromosomes as well as genes occur in pair.

items.answer: The Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance was consistent with Mendel's laws and was supported by the following observations: (a) during meiosis, homologous chromosome pairs migrate as discrete structures that are independent of other chromosome pairs; (b) the sorting of chromosomes from each homologous pair into pre-gametes appears to be random; (c) each parent synthesizes gametes that contain only half of their chromosomal complement; (d) even though male and female gametes (sperm and egg) differ in size and morphology, they have the same number of chromosomes, suggesting equal genetic contributions from each parent. Thus (a) is the correct option.
items.ocr: The label of option (c) was lost by MinerU ('The two alleles of a gene pair...' printed with no letter) and was restored from the surviving (a), (b) and (d) sequence. The tail of the worked solution (observation (d)) and the printed key 'Thus (a) is the correct option' are not adjacent to the question in the markdown: MinerU emitted this book page as '## Page 3' and the page that continues it as '## Page 2', so the key is at the top of the Page 2 block. It reads (a), which is what correct_option records.

items.stem: Exchange of genetic material takes place in
items.answer: (c) sexual reproduction. In sexual reproduction two gametes from two different parents fuse, so genetic material from both parents is combined in the offspring.
items.ocr: Label '(c)' was dropped before 'sexual reproduction' in the option list; restored from the printed answer '(c) sexual reproduction'.

items.stem: Two pink coloured flowers on crossing resulted in 1 red, 2 pink and 1 white flower progeny. The nature of the cross will be
items.answer: (b) self pollination. The 1 : 2 : 1 ratio of red : pink : white is the F₂ ratio of a monohybrid cross between two identical heterozygous (pink) parents, which happens when the pink flowers are self pollinated.

items.stem: A cross between a tall plant (TT) and short pea plant (tt) resulted in progeny that were all tall plants because

options.label: D
options.text: height of pea plant is not governed by gene 'T' or 't'

items.answer: (a) tallness is the dominant trait. All the F₁ plants are Tt; they are tall because the factor T for tallness dominates the factor t for dwarfness.

items.stem: Which of the following statement is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: For every hormone there is a gene.

options.label: B
options.text: For every protein there is a gene.

options.label: C
options.text: For production of every enzyme there is a gene.

options.label: D
options.text: For every molecule of fat there is a gene.

items.answer: (d) For every molecule of fat there is a gene. Genes carry information for making proteins (including hormones and enzymes); fats are not directly coded by genes, they are made by enzymes which are themselves gene products.

items.stem: A round, green seeded pea plant (RRyy) is crossed with wrinkled, yellow seeded pea plant (rrYY), the seeds produced in F₁ generation are
items.answer: (a) round and yellow. The F₁ plants are RrYy; round (R) is dominant over wrinkled (r) and yellow (Y) is dominant over green (y), so all F₁ seeds are round and yellow.
items.ocr: LaTeX '$\mathrm{~F~}_{1}$' rewritten as F₁; the spaced genotypes 'RR yy' and 'rr YY' closed up to RRyy and rrYY.

items.stem:
In human males all the chromosomes are paired perfectly except one. This/these unpaired chromosomes is/are
(i) large chromosomes
(ii) small chromosomes
(iii) Y-chromosome
(iv) X-chromosome
items.answer: (c) (iii) and (iv). A human male carries one X and one Y chromosome; these two are not a perfectly matched pair, so both the X and the Y remain unpaired in the male.
items.ocr: Stem printed as 'Human males all the chromosomes are paired...'; the dropped opening word 'In' was restored.

items.stem: The maleness of a child is determined by

options.label: A
options.text: the X chromosome in the zygote

options.label: C
options.text: the cytoplasm of germ cell which determines the sex

items.answer: (b) the Y chromosome in zygote. A zygote that receives a Y chromosome from the father becomes a male child.

items.stem: A zygote which has an X-chromosome inherited from the father will develop into a

options.label: C
options.text: X-chromosome does not determine the sex of a child

items.answer: (b) girl. The mother always contributes an X chromosome, so a zygote that also receives an X chromosome from the father is XX and develops into a girl.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : The sex of the children will be determined by chromosome received from the father.
Reason (R) : A human male has one X and one Y-chromosome.
items.assertion: The sex of the children will be determined by chromosome received from the father.
items.reason: A human male has one X and one Y-chromosome.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: (a) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A). A child who inherits the X-chromosome from the father will be a girl and one who inherits a Y-chromosome will be a boy.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : Changes in non-reproductive tissues can be passed on the DNA of the germ cells.
Reason (R) : Inherited traits include the traits developed during the lifetime of an individual that cannot be passed on to its progeny.
items.assertion: Changes in non-reproductive tissues can be passed on the DNA of the germ cells.
items.reason: Inherited traits include the traits developed during the lifetime of an individual that cannot be passed on to its progeny.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: (d) Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true. Changes in non-reproductive tissues cannot be passed on to the DNA of the germ cells. The traits that develop during the lifetime of an individual and cannot be passed on to the progeny are acquired traits.
items.ocr: Answer-key tension recorded, not altered: the book prints 'Ans : (d)' (assertion false, reason true) but its own worked solution says the traits developed during a lifetime are ACQUIRED traits, which makes the printed reason (calling them 'inherited traits') false as well. The printed key (d) is kept because the solution names no other option and the four-option legend has no 'both false' choice.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : Chromosomes are known as hereditary vehicles.
Reason (R) : The chromosomes are capable of self-reproduction and maintaining morphological and physiological properties through successive generations.
items.assertion: Chromosomes are known as hereditary vehicles.
items.reason: The chromosomes are capable of self-reproduction and maintaining morphological and physiological properties through successive generations.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: (a) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A). Chromosomes carry the genes from one generation to the next, and because they can self-replicate they preserve the morphological and physiological characters of the species through successive generations.

Reason (R) : A DNA finger print is inherited and therefore, resembles that of parents.

items.answer: (a) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A). DNA fingerprinting amplifies DNA by the polymerase chain reaction and then detects specific sequences with DNA probes; because DNA is inherited from both parents, an individual's fingerprint pattern resembles that of the parents.

items.stem: Write the sex chromosome in woman and man.
items.answer: In woman: XX. In man: XY.

items.stem: Define mutation.
items.answer: Sudden changes in the genetic form of an organism which are passed on to the next generation are called mutations.

items.stem: Name the first Indian medical practitioner who was aware of the concepts of genetics.
items.answer: Charaka was the first Indian medical practitioner who knew the factors which determine the sex of the child.

items.stem: Which of the following traits are recessive in pea plant? Dwarfness, violet flower, wrinkled seed.
items.answer: Dwarfness and wrinkled seeds are the recessive characters.

items.stem: How is the female produced ?
items.answer: When a sperm carrying the X chromosome from the father fertilizes the egg, then a female (girl) is produced.

items.stem: How many types of chromosomes are there in the cell?
items.answer: There are two types of chromosomes in the cell: (i) sex chromosomes, and (ii) autosomes.

items.stem: Do a tailless mice have a tailless progeny ?
items.answer: No, because removal of the tail is an acquired trait and cannot change the genes of the germ cells of the mice.
items.ocr: Answer printed 'a quired trait'; corrected to 'acquired trait'.

items.stem: Name the biological term used to show differences among individuals.
items.answer: Variation.

items.stem: How many pairs of chromosomes are present in human beings?
items.answer: 23 pairs.

items.stem: Name the type of chromosomes which helps in the determination of sex in an organism.
items.answer: Sex chromosomes or allosomes.

items.stem: What are traits ?
items.answer: The characters in individuals are called traits.

items.stem: In a mono-hybrid cross a round seeded plant was crossed with a wrinkle seeded plant. In F₂ generation genotype ratio obtained was 1 : 2 : 1. How many plants were homozygous round?
items.answer: A quarter of the plants (25%) were homozygous round.
items.ocr: LaTeX '$\mathrm{{F_{2}}}$' rewritten as F₂; the missing question mark was added to the printed stem.

items.stem: Name the plant on which Mendel performed his experiments.
items.answer: Mendel performed his experiments on garden pea (Pisum sativum).

items.stem: What is F₂ generation?
items.answer: The generation produced by the offspring of the F₁ generation, i.e. taking the first generation as the parent, is called the F₂ or second generation.
items.ocr: LaTeX '$\mathrm{{F_{2}}}$' and '$\mathrm{F}_{1}$' rewritten as F₂ and F₁.

items.stem:
(a) What is the genetic constitution of human sperm?
(b) Mention the chromosome pair present in the zygote determining the sex of a male child.
items.answer:
(a) 22 + Y or 22 + X.
(b) 22 + Y and 22 + X, or 44 + XY.
items.ocr: LaTeX '$22+\mathrm{X}$', '$\mathrm{22+Y}$' and '$44+\mathrm{XY}$' rewritten as plain 22 + X, 22 + Y and 44 + XY; 'determing' corrected to 'determining'.

items.stem: Define a gene.
items.answer: A gene is a segment of functional DNA on a chromosome occupying a specific position which codes for a specific trait or protein synthesis. As such, it is a heredity determinant or a unit of genetic information.
